setting.placeName:
United States Legation,
Rio de Janeiro

opener.dateline:
United States Legation,
Rio de Janeiro, September 27, 1871.

div.p:
To the Councilor Mr. Manoel Francisco Correia,
Minister and Secretary of State, &c., &c, &c.:

I have received the dispatch (No. 3887) dated on the 23d September, in which the councilor and secretary of state, Senhor Manoel Francisco Correia, minister of foreign affairs, informs me that Her highness the princess imperial, regent, in name of His Majesty the Emperor, has been pleased to appoint the Baron de Itajubá, of His Majesty’s council, and now envoy extraordinary and minister plenipotentiary in France, as a member of the tribunal of arbitration, under the first article of the treaty of Washington.

I have, by the packet of the 24th instant, already communicated this information to the honorable the Secretary of State at Washington, and I do not doubt that the President of the United States will learn with satisfaction the appointment of the Baron de Itajubá, who has so distinguished a reputation for learning and impartiality, which reputation, added to the confidence of the Emperor, of itself a high proof of his merits, ought to render such nomination entirely acceptable to both the powers concerned.

I desire to thank the councilor, Mr. Correia, for his promptness in making known to me this appointment in time for the packet, and I avail myself of the occasion to renew the assurances of my complete consideration.
